# Qwik v2 agents reference, instructions and rules

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **ALWAYS RUN `ruler apply` AT THE START OF A SESSION.** The agent skills are gitignored, not
> committed, so a fresh clone/worktree has none until you generate them (once per worktree):
>
> ```bash
> pnpm dlx @intellectronica/ruler@0.3.42 apply --no-gitignore --no-mcp
> ```

> Canonical source for repo-wide AI coding agent rules. For contributor setup, see
> [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). For package-specific workflows, load the relevant
> `.ruler/skills/*/SKILL.md` file.

## Source Of Truth

- Shared AI guidance lives in `.ruler/`.
- Only the root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are committed generated outputs; the `.claude/`/`.codex/`
  skill copies are gitignored and regenerated locally with `ruler apply` (see Setup below).
- Never hand-edit a generated output — edit `.ruler/` and regenerate with `ruler apply`. A CI check
  re-runs it and fails if the committed root files drift.
- To change assistant behavior, edit `.ruler/AGENTS.md`, `.ruler/README.md`, or `.ruler/skills/**`,
  then regenerate with Ruler when needed.

## Project Snapshot

Qwik is a resumable web framework. SSR serializes application and framework state into HTML, and
the client resumes without re-running component code. Qwik v2 is a rewrite with VNode-based
runtime work, rewritten reactive primitives, a new serialization mechanism, and package names under
`@qwik.dev/*`.

Key concepts: resumability, QRLs, `$`-suffixed optimizer boundaries, fine-grained signals, VNodes,
the cursor system, and the Rust optimizer.

## Monorepo Map

- Base branch and release branch for v2 PRs: `main`. V1 lives on the `v1` branch.

| Package | Path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@qwik.dev/core` | `packages/qwik` | Core runtime, SSR, optimizer-facing code |
| `@qwik.dev/router` | `packages/qwik-router` | Routing, middleware, adapters, SSG |
| `@qwik.dev/react` | `packages/qwik-react` | React integration |
| `@qwik.dev/utils` | `packages/qwik-utils` | Less-common helpers (`usePoll`, `zod$`), may use qwik internals |
| `@qwik.dev/dom` | `packages/qwik-dom` | Server-side DOM implementation |
| `@qwik.dev/qwik-vite` | `packages/qwik-vite` | `vite-plugin-qwik`, private, bundled into `@qwik.dev/core/optimizer` |
| `@qwik.dev/ts-optimizer` | `packages/ts-optimizer` | TypeScript optimizer, private, bundled into `@qwik.dev/core/optimizer` |
| `@qwik.dev/optimizer` | `packages/optimizer` | Rust optimizer, WASM, NAPI bindings; kept for parity comparison |
| `eslint-plugin-qwik` | `packages/eslint-plugin-qwik` | ESLint rules |
| `create-qwik` | `packages/create-qwik` | Project scaffolding CLI |
| `qwik-docs` | `packages/docs` | Docs site, private package |
| `insights` | `packages/insights` | Analytics dashboard, private package |

Use v2 package names (`@qwik.dev/core`, `@qwik.dev/router`, etc.). Do not introduce v1
`@builder.io/qwik` or `@builder.io/qwik-city` imports except when working on explicit
compatibility override code.

## Setup And Iteration Loop

This is the canonical loop for nearly all framework work. Default to it; do not substitute broader
commands:

### getting started

```bash
pnpm i
```

```bash
# Materialize the agent skills into .claude/.codex (gitignored) — run once per fresh clone/worktree.
pnpm dlx @intellectronica/ruler@0.3.42 apply --no-gitignore --no-mcp
```

```bash
pnpm build.core # for a fresh start
pnpm build.full # for a fresh start and you are working on the docs or the other packages
pnpm build.rust # only when working on the Rust optimizer; the only step that needs the Rust toolchain
```

The local scripts and tests use the TypeScript optimizer (`tsOptimizer: true` in the repo's own
vite configs and test harnesses), so no Rust toolchain or prebuilt bindings are needed for them.
Keep that flag on any new repo-owned `qwikVite()` call site; the plugin still defaults to the Rust
optimizer for published apps. `QWIK_OPTIMIZER=rust` (or `ts`) overrides the flag for a whole run, which
is how CI runs the e2e suites on both optimizers; it needs `pnpm build.rust` or
`pnpm build.platform.copy` first.
### Iterating

Prefer focused commands and builds over repo-wide commands and builds.

```bash
# Fast dev build — required once before any tests can run, and again after framework
# source changes when the verification consumes build output (all e2e suites do)
pnpm build.core.dev

# Closest focused unit/spec test
pnpm vitest run packages/qwik/src/core/tests/use-task.spec.tsx

# Focused e2e test
pnpm playwright test e2e/qwik-e2e/tests/events.e2e.ts --browser=chromium --config e2e/qwik-e2e/playwright.config.ts
```

`build.core.dev` also re-emits fresh Qwik and Router `.d.ts` incrementally (via `tscDevDts` + re-export shims), so editing a public signature no longer leaves stale types — `build.watch` skips the type pass to stay instant.

For Qwik e2e tests, use `--browser=chromium` with `e2e/qwik-e2e/playwright.config.ts`.

Re-run `pnpm build.rust` (or `pnpm build.rust.dev`) when you are touching the optimizer rust code.

### When making a PR

```bash
# for type-level verification when no focused test covers the change
pnpm tsc.check

# update the API
pnpm api.update

# Verify the build passes
pnpm build.core

# Verify unit tests pass
pnpm test.unit

# Verify the E2Es pass
pnpm test.e2e.chromium

# In case of html output change, update the ssg snapshot
pnpm test.e2e.router.ssg.update

# In case of a new feature, run the test.bench
pnpm test.bench

# In case of qwikloader changes
pnpm vitest packages/qwik/src/qwikloader.unit.ts -u
```

If any of those fail, fix and push your changes.

## Rules

Recent Qwik v2 work by core maintainers favors small, behavior-shaped changes with regression proof.
Follow that bias:

### Guidance Freshness

- If a skill or reference you used is stale, incomplete, or contradicted by current source, update
  the `.ruler` source guidance before finishing the task unless the user explicitly restricted the
  scope.
- Keep new durable lessons in the most specific skill or reference that future agents are likely to
  load. Do not add package-specific details to these always-on rules unless they affect most tasks.
- Only add a lesson to a skill when it generalizes to future tasks. Keep single-PR specifics (one
  module's protocol, one fix's mechanics) in the code and its tests, not in a skill.
- Write those notes **prescriptively** — the invariants to keep, the traps that cause false passes,
  where things live, and how to verify — rather than describing how the code currently works. Omit "don't do X" prohibitions for anything a test already enforces; the
  suite is the guardrail, so reserve notes for what it can't self-enforce.
- When updating guidance, load the `qwik-guidance-maintenance` skill.

### Skill Selection

Load the relevant skill before non-trivial work in that area:

| Skill | Use when |
| --- | --- |
| `qwik-core-development` | Editing/reviewing `packages/qwik/**` core runtime code |
| `qwik-router-development` | Editing/reviewing router runtime, buildtime, middleware, adapters, or SSG |
| `qwik-optimizer-development` | Editing/reviewing Rust optimizer, WASM, NAPI, or optimizer-facing behavior |
| `qwik-e2e-verification` | Creating, debugging, or running Playwright e2e suites |
| `qwik-docs-development` | Writing/editing docs content, docs site routes, or docs LLM outputs |
| `qwik-guidance-maintenance` | Editing `.ruler/**`, generated-output guidance, or stale skill/reference content |

If no skill fits, stay with these repo-wide rules and inspect local source before changing code.

If a skill above is not loadable, its copy has not been generated in this worktree yet — run the
`ruler apply` step from Setup, or read the source directly at `.ruler/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.

Keep the `qwik-` prefix on committed source skill names. Ruler copies these skills into
agent-native skill directories where they may coexist with user or plugin skills, so the prefix keeps
the skill list unambiguous outside the repo-local `.ruler` tree.

# Contributing to Qwik

Thank you for taking an interest in contributing to Qwik! We appreciate you! 🫶🏽

Below are the guidelines on how to help in the best possible way.

## Submitting an Issue

Before creating a new issue, please search through open issues using the [GitHub issue search bar](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/filtering-and-searching-issues-and-pull-requests). You might find the solution to your problem, or can verify that it is an already known issue.

We want a bug-free and best-performing project. That's why we take all reported issues to heart. But please be aware that if we can't reproduce the problem, we won't have a way of locating and adequately fixing it.

Therefore, to solve the problem in the best possible way, please create a minimal repository that reproduces the problem with the least possible code explaining and demonstrating the error.

Without enough information to reproduce the issue, we will close it because we can't recreate and solve it.

## Triaging Issues

If you're interested in helping out with triaging issues, please follow the [Triaging Guide](./contributing/TRIAGE.md).

## Submitting a Pull Request (PR)

### Branch Organization

We adopt [trunk-based development](https://trunkbaseddevelopment.com/) therefore all Pull Requests are made against the main branch.
Before releasing, we merge `main` into a release branch, for testing purposes.

### Good first issue

The issues marked with [_Good first issue_](https://github.com/QwikDev/qwik/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22COMMUNITY%3A++good+first+issue%22) are a good starting point to familiarize yourself with the project.

Before solving the problem, please check with the maintainers that the issue is still relevant. Feel free to leave a comment on the issue to show your intention to work on it and prevent other people from unintentionally duplicating your effort.

### Sending a Pull Request

Before submitting a pull request, consider the following guidelines:

- Fork the repository into your own account.
- In your forked repository, create a new branch: `git checkout -b my-branch main`
- Make your changes/fixes.
- Run `pnpm fmt` to lint the code.
- Add a changeset with `pnpm change` if needed ([follow this tutorial](https://go.screenpal.com/watch/cZivIcVPJQV))
- Push your branch to GitHub: `git push origin my-branch`
- In GitHub, send a pull request to `QwikDev:main`.

> If you aren't sure your PR is ready, open it as a [draft](https://github.blog/2019-02-14-introducing-draft-pull-requests/) to make it clear to the maintainer.

### ⚠ Troubleshooting PR build issues on CI

Every PR is being automatically merged with `main` before the CI Github actions run.
That's why if the CI checks aren't passing your PR branch is probably not up to date.

**For non documentation PRs please do the following:**

1. Merge `main` into your PR branch
2. Run `pnpm api.update`
3. Run `pnpm build.full` (add `pnpm build.rust` if you made a change to the Rust code)
4. Commit and push any changes as a result of the above steps

## Local development

This is the best approach because all required dependencies will be installed in the docker container for you and won't affect your personal configuration in any way.

### Prerequisites

You need to have these tools up and running in your local machine:

- an editor. We recommend [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/).
- one of the following:
  - [Nix](https://nixos.org)
  - [Docker](https://www.docker.com/)
  - Locally installed NodeJS v22+ (Rust is only needed for the Rust optimizer, see below)

#### Nix

[Nix](https://nixos.org/download.html) can be used on macOS and Linux. It keeps installation files in `/nix` and doesn't write anywhere else. It has a declarative configuration in the `flake.nix` file, which describes all the tools needed to build the project.

- Install it on your machine and enable flakes. The [DetSys installer](https://github.com/DeterminateSystems/nix-installer) makes that easy.
- run `nix develop` in the project root to open a shell with all the tools, or use `direnv` to have them automatically added into your current shell.

##### Nix + Direnv (optional)

You can additionally use [direnv](https://direnv.net/) to automatically load the dev environment when you enter the project directory.
There is also a VSCode plugin for direnv that reloads the extensions so they get environment changes.
When you install direnv, you'll need to allow it once with `direnv allow` in the project root. From then on, when you `cd` into the project, it will automatically have the correct tools installed.

#### Docker

- Install the [Dev Containers](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers) extension in your VSCode.
- Once installed you will be prompted to 'Reopen the folder to develop in a container [learn more](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/devcontainers/containers) or Clone repository in Docker volume for [better I/O performance](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/devcontainers/containers#_quick-start-open-a-git-repository-or-github-pr-in-an-isolated-container-volume)'. If you're not prompted, you can run the `Dev Containers: Open Folder in Container` command from the [VSCode Command Palette](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/userinterface#_command-palette).

Alternatively you can use [devcontainers/cli](https://github.com/devcontainers/cli):

- Install devcontainers following their documentation.
- In your terminal navigate to the Qwik's project root directory.
- Then run `devcontainer up --workspace-folder .`. This command will start a Docker container with all required environment dependencies.

> [!TIP]
> If you are using Podman, be sure to update the [VSCode dev container settings](https://code.visualstudio.com/remote/advancedcontainers/docker-options#_podman). Don't forget to allocate enough resources to the Podman machine to avoid slow builds.

> [!NOTE]
> You may run into an `EEXISTS` error when the Dev Container runs the "updateContentCommand" script. This may happen if pnpm gets installed automatically during the setup process. You can ignore the error because the container will be setup correctly, then run `pnpm install` in the project root once the container is connected and the terminal is available.

> [!CAUTION]
> The Dev Container may not work on Windows properly due to a difference with Windows container host volume permissions and ownership. It's recommended to use Mac or Linux instead, or configure your environment to build the project without Dev Containers.

##### Using development container without Dev Containers and VSCode

If you would like to make use of the development container solution, but don't use VSCode or Dev Containers, you still can do so, by following steps:

- Build development container locally: `cd .devcontainer; docker build -t qwik-container .`
- Run development container from Qwik project root, binding the directory to container: `cd ..; docker run --rm -d --name qwik-container -p 3300:3300 -p 9229:9299 -v $PWD:/home/circleci/project -t qwik-container`

Docker command does:

- Create a new container that is removed once stopped,
- In daemon mode,
- With name `qwik-container`,
- That exposes the ports `3300` and `9229`, and
- Binds `qwik` project directory to container working directory.

Instant-loading web apps, without effort

This is the branch for Qwik v2, currently in beta. For v1, see the `v1` branch. Qwik offers the fastest possible page load times - regardless of the complexity of your website. Qwik is so fast because it allows fully interactive sites to load with almost no JavaScript and [pick up from where the server left off](https://next.qwik.dev/docs/concepts/resumable/). As users interact with the site, only the necessary parts of the site load on-demand. This [precision lazy-loading](https://next.qwik.dev/docs/concepts/progressive/) is what makes Qwik so quick. ## Getting Started ```sh npm create qwik@beta # or pnpm create qwik@beta # or yarn create qwik@beta # or bun create qwik@beta ``` - Understand the difference between [resumable and replayable](https://next.qwik.dev/docs/concepts/resumable/) applications. - Learn about Qwik's high level [mental model](https://next.qwik.dev/docs/concepts/think-qwik/). ## Nightlies We use pkg.pr.new to make packages available for each PR and for the branches. Use these URLs instead of versions to get the latest build: - https://pkg.pr.new/QwikDev/qwik/@qwik.dev/core@main - https://pkg.pr.new/QwikDev/qwik/@qwik.dev/router@main - https://pkg.pr.new/QwikDev/qwik/@qwik.dev/react@main - https://pkg.pr.new/QwikDev/qwik/@qwik.dev/devtools@main ## Resources - [Docs](https://next.qwik.dev/) - [Examples](https://next.qwik.dev/examples/introduction/hello-world/) - [Tutorials](https://next.qwik.dev/tutorial/welcome/overview/) - [Videos](https://next.qwik.dev/media/#videos) - [Podcasts](https://next.qwik.dev/media/#podcasts) - [Presentations](https://next.qwik.dev/media/#presentations) - [Blogs](https://next.qwik.dev/media/#blogs) ## Community - Ping us at [@QwikDev](https://twitter.com/QwikDev) - Join our [Discord](https://qwik.dev/chat) community - Join all the [other community groups](https://next.qwik.dev/ecosystem/#community) ## Development - See [Contributing.md](https://github.com/QwikDev/qwik/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information on how to build Qwik from the source and contribute! ## Related - [Partytown](https://partytown.qwik.dev/): Relocate resource intensive third-party scripts off of the main thread and into a web worker 🎉. - [Mitosis](https://github.com/BuilderIO/mitosis): Write components once, run everywhere. report.overview: Qwik v2 is a web framework for developers building server-rendered applications that resume execution from serialized state and load event code on demand. This monorepo contains the reactive runtime, SSR engine, TypeScript and Rust optimizers, routing and deployment adapters, project scaffolding, React integration, developer inspection tools, and an Insights analytics application. Its distinctive architecture connects extracted QRL functions, build manifests, HTML metadata, and lazily restored client state. This brief reflects bounded, read-only inspection at commit 8eb4589be115eb8f2dabfd12c107dcc23647caec; no repository code, tests, builds, or workflows were executed.
report.agent_prompt:
You are onboarding to Qwik at commit 8eb4589be115eb8f2dabfd12c107dcc23647caec on main. Treat this as the v2 codebase and use @qwik.dev/core and @qwik.dev/router names. Qwik resumes from server-serialized state; describe its own runtime using resumability terminology. The inspected system includes a framework and supporting applications, so identify the owning package before investigating an issue.

Start with AGENTS.md, package.json, the relevant package manifest, and the smallest implementation and test files that explain the requested behavior. Shared guidance originates in .ruler; AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are generated outputs. For this read-only investigation, do not run Ruler, install dependencies, execute repository code, start browsers or servers, or modify files. Prefix shell read/search commands with rtk. Never inspect .env files, credentials, or keys. If a later task authorizes implementation, reassess its execution permissions before using the documented contributor workflow.

Core public APIs are exported from packages/qwik/src/core/index.ts. Follow SSR through server/ssr-render.ts into server/ssr-container.ts. The container emits paused-container attributes, serialized state, event metadata, and function references. Read core/shared/serdes/serialization.md before changing the encoding. DomContainer processes VNode metadata and qwik/state scripts; state restoration can use a lazy deserializer proxy. Browser events begin in qwikloader.ts, which registers scoped listeners, waits for streamed-container readiness, resolves handler chunks, and invokes captures. core/client/run-qrl.ts restores invocation context, while SignalImpl records subscriptions and schedules effects when values change.

Router work crosses runtime, buildtime, and middleware boundaries. The Vite plugin generates route configuration and entries. Node middleware converts HTTP requests into request events; requestHandler loads configuration and routes, resolveRequestHandlers orders middleware, and runQwikRouter drives execution. Read both actionHandler and submitAction for action protocol changes. Loader endpoints use q-loader-{id}.{manifestHash}.json and Qwik custom serialization despite their JSON-looking URLs. Preserve origin checks, internal-path validation, request-body limits, redirects, and cache eligibility rules.

Scaffolding starts in create-qwik/index.ts, discovers packaged integration metadata, composes templates through createApp, stages updateApp file changes, and optionally runs package-manager installation. Insights is separate: GitHub authentication protects dashboard access, while validated telemetry updates libSQL tables through Drizzle. Its ingestion response precedes awaited database updates, and statistical counters deliberately avoid transactions.

Tests and CI were inspected, not executed; their existence proves intended coverage only. Vitest covers runtime and request protocols, Playwright covers browser behavior, and Rust transforms use Insta snapshots. Future authorized verification should begin with the closest focused test after required build artifacts exist. Keep diffs scoped, preserve unrelated work, and cite exact tracked files and concise line ranges. Do not turn this bounded inventory into whole-repository absence claims or label source hypotheses as confirmed vulnerabilities.

system_map.summary: The repository distributes a framework through several packages rather than running as one application. Core exposes separate client, server, optimizer, and CLI surfaces, while Router connects generated route configuration to platform middleware. Supporting applications include documentation and Insights, and development tooling includes MCP inspection. Build and deployment commands below are source-defined capabilities, not commands executed during this investigation.

claims.claim: The pinned branch describes Qwik v2 as resumable, with VNode runtime work, rewritten reactive primitives, and a new serialization mechanism.
@qwik.dev/core publishes conditional development/production runtime exports, an internal surface, JSX runtime exports, and a qwik CLI executable.
renderToString delegates to renderToStream; streaming creates an SSRContainer, installs the server platform, renders JSX, and flushes buffered output.
Browser startup is owned by qwikloader.ts, which turns window._qwikEv into a registration object and installs scoped event listeners.
Router has buildtime-generated virtual modules and shared runtime route matching; requestHandler is the request entry used by adapters.
createQwikPlugin selects @qwik.dev/ts-optimizer or @qwik.dev/optimizer; QWIK_OPTIMIZER=ts|rust overrides the option and invalid values throw.
The Rust workspace includes optimizer core and NAPI members, lists then excludes the WASM member, and configures a size-oriented release profile.
Insights owns persistent application, symbol, error, and manifest tables through Drizzle's libSQL database type and an initialized module-level database handle.
The workspace spans packages/* and e2e/*, requires strict engine compatibility, and pins pnpm 11.22.0 with Node >=22.18.0 at the root.
Root build.core.dev, build.full, test.unit, and browser-specific test scripts define the contributor build/test surface; docs deployment consumes CI artifacts and publishes to Cloudflare Pages.

feature_catalog.summary: The primary user is an application developer using components, reactive state, routing, server functions, and deployment adapters. The inspected public surfaces also provide scaffolding, React interoperability, lint rules, and local inspection tools. Insights adds telemetry ingestion and an authenticated dashboard foundation. This catalog covers evidenced feature families; the capped inventory and selective source reads do not establish an exhaustive list of every example, documentation screen, or integration.

claims.claim: Core exports component$, QRL boundaries $, sync$, event$, JSX helpers, Slot, and client rendering APIs.
Developer state APIs include useStore, useSignal, computed signals, async signals, contexts, scoped styles, tasks, visible tasks, resources, and serializers.
Each, Show, Pending, and Catch are exposed control-flow/error primitives; optimizer experimental flags include each, show, pendingBoundary, catchBoundary, and blockSSR.
Event handling supports element, document, and window scopes, passive variants, preventdefault attributes, stoppropagation attributes, and late registrations.
routeLoader$ supplies ComputedSignal data, per-loader endpoints, search-parameter allowlists, ETags, cache-control options, and strict-loader defaults.
Route actions provide browser submission state and form completion events; JSON action handling runs validators and can return explicit loader invalidation hashes.
server-function requests can return either a serialized value or an async-iterator stream using application/qwik-json and text/qwik-json-stream.
Router exposes adapters for Azure SWA, Cloudflare Pages, Cloud Run, Bun, Deno, Node, Netlify Edge, static generation, and Vercel Edge.
create-qwik supports argument-based or interactive startup; the argument path accepts template, output directory, --force, and --installDeps.
React interoperability exports qwikify$ and reactify$; qwikifyQrl tracks props, resolves the React component lazily, maintains a React root, and schedules root cleanup.
Developer tooling includes recommended/strict ESLint rule sets and MCP tools for project information, route lists, browser errors, page inspection, and offline documentation.
Insights accepts symbol timing telemetry, mounts an Insights component and RouterOutlet, and integrates GitHub sign-in, sign-out, and session APIs.

data_flow.summary: Qwik transforms application code into addressable functions and associates runtime references with build manifests. SSR emits HTML plus container and state metadata, which the client consumes when execution resumes. Router transports action and loader results through Qwik serialization, while Insights converts validated telemetry into statistical database updates. Scaffolding follows a separate filesystem path that stages template merges and optionally invokes a package manager.

claims.claim: Optimizer extraction records immutable symbol names, hashes, canonical filenames, byte offsets, body text, and QRL callee metadata for subsequent pipeline phases.
resolveManifest merges the built and supplied manifests, then maps symbol hashes to symbol names and bundle filenames.
SSR openContainer emits paused state, runtime version, build base, locale, manifest hash, and instance hash as container attributes.
emitStateData directs the serialization context into the SSR writer inside a qwik/state script; eager-resume roots add an idle-event QRL.

The documented state representation alternates type identifiers and encoded values, references shared roots, resolves promise forward references, and restores objects through allocation and inflation.
DomContainer parses qwik/state, preprocesses roots, chooses eager restoration or wrapDeserializerProxy, processes segment state when enabled, and marks the container resumed.
Event attributes encode chunk, symbol, and capture IDs; dispatch resolves the chunk relative to q:base and invokes the handler with capture IDs as its this value.
SignalImpl.value reads register effect subscriptions and back references; changed writes update the stored value and call scheduleEffects.
submitAction sends FormData or JSON to ?qaction=ID and decodes the response with _deserialize; actionHandler serializes result and optional loaderHashes.
fetchRouteLoaderData constructs a manifest-versioned loader URL, optionally forwards the page path, caches requests by URL and full-path header, and handles redirects and aborts.
Insights parses incoming JSON with InsightsPayload, normalizes symbol names, buckets delay/latency/timeline measurements, and passes application/manifest identifiers into updateEdge and updateRoutes.
createFromStarter writes initial package metadata and README, stages base and optional starter integrations through updateApp, and applies their filesystem writes through commit callbacks.

behavior_traces.summary: Four concrete flows were followed across their owning files: a server-rendered page and resumed event, a route action, project scaffolding, and Insights ingestion. These traces describe source control flow rather than observed runtime executions. They expose explicit synchronization points: SSR flushes, streamed-container readiness, action submission serialization, and database writes after response creation.

claims.claim: Page request, step 1: createQwikRouter.router computes the origin, combines body limits, calls fromNodeHttp, and passes the resulting event to requestHandler.
Page request, step 2: requestHandler obtains getRouterConfig, loads routes through loadRequestHandlers/loadRoute, resolves middleware, and calls runQwikRouter.

Page request, step 3: runQwikRouter creates RequestEvent and drives runNext; page middleware runs actions/loaders before renderQwikMiddleware supplies serverData and a stream to the application's render function.
SSR step: renderToStream resolves manifest/base, creates StreamHandler and SSRContainer, calls setServerPlatform and container.render, awaits the render promise, then flushes.
Resumed click step: qwikloader dispatch reads q-e:click, locates the container, waits for its ready marker when streaming, resolves/imports the handler, and invokes it with captured IDs.

QRL invocation step: _run obtains DomContainer, waits for container data, creates invocation context, deserializes capture deltas, and calls runEventHandlerQRL; that function inflates the host element and invokes through retryOnPromise.

Action flow: routeActionQrl.submit queues behind pendingDispatch and updates currentAction; the router task calls submitAction, actionHandler parses/validates/calls the QRL, and the client receives result plus invalidation hashes.
Scaffold flow: create-qwik.mjs calls runCli; arguments choose runCreateCli, which builds a template manager, validates the target-directory policy, and invokes createApp.
Scaffold write/install flow: createApp calls createFromStarter, updateApp merges integration files, commit creates directories and writes files, and installDeps delegates to runCommand using execa.

Insights persistence flow: plugin@db initializes the libSQL client; onPost parses and validates telemetry, sends an OK response, then resolves manifest/application records and awaits updateEdge/updateRoutes counter updates or inserts.

testing_signals.summary: Tests and CI configuration were inspected, not executed; test existence is not a passing result. Vitest exercises package-level specifications, Playwright exercises browser and adapter behavior, and Rust optimizer tests use Insta snapshots. Inspected tests provide concrete coverage signals for serialization, streamed events, action responses, request limits, and database aggregation. Coverage remains bounded: this investigation did not establish complete test coverage or production behavior.

claims.claim: The inspected root Vitest configuration includes package *.spec.* and *.unit.* files, excludes generated/dependency trees, loads vitest-setup.ts, and enables the TypeScript optimizer.
Serialization tests snapshot encoded Plain and RootRef values and separately test decoding; additional assertions restore signal effect back references and compute QRLs.
qwikloader.behavior.unit.ts reads dist/qwikloader.debug.js and executes it inside mocked browser globals, so its intended checks depend on current build output.
A loader regression test asserts that a click does not run before streamed-container data is ready and runs after QwikEvContainerReady is pushed.
Playwright events.e2e.ts checks independent counter updates, prevented navigation, propagation behavior, and mouseleave/mouseover execution ordering.
Action-handler unit tests deserialize response bodies and assert default, explicit, and strict-mode invalidation semantics plus validator failure status.
Request-body-limit tests cover exact-limit acceptance, oversized single/multiple chunks, and invalid limit configuration.
Insights query tests use an in-memory libSQL client with explicit fixtures to check cross-manifest aggregation and isolation from another application's rows.
Rust test_input_fn invokes transform_modules and snapshot_res records emitted modules, maps, segment metadata, and diagnostics using insta::assert_snapshot!.
Core Playwright configuration uses *.e2e.ts, parallel execution, a localhost dev-server command, CI-only traces/screenshots, and forbidOnly; docs use a separate Chromium configuration.
Inspected CI defines unit and MCP checks plus sharded browser runs with QWIK_OPTIMIZER set from TS/Rust matrix entries; no CI run result was retrieved.

The inspected action unit harness mocks parseBody and QRL execution, and the Insights query fixtures test reads rather than the full authenticated ingestion path; those tests alone do not prove those integrations.

risk_map.summary: The main sensitive boundaries are HTML/script generation, browser chunk loading, request routing and execution, scaffold filesystem writes, local inspection IPC, and privileged CI deployment. Concrete guards exist at several boundaries, including escaping, origin validation, byte limits, and loopback/token checks. Source inconsistencies and operational hypotheses below are not confirmed vulnerabilities. No runtime exploit, production configuration, credential value, or whole-repository absence was established.

claims.claim: SSR escapes ordinary text and attribute values, while htmlNode writes raw HTML and dangerouslySetInnerHTML preserves supplied HTML; callers choosing raw output own a sensitive trust boundary.
Backpatch scripts replace '<' with a Unicode escape and apply a supplied nonce; sync-function scripts also propagate serverData.nonce.
Browser resolveHandler imports a URL derived from chunk metadata and q:base, then selects a named export; integrity of server-emitted QRL metadata is therefore a code-loading boundary.
Router enables checkOrigin by default and prepends CSRF checks for mutation methods; the check compares origins for simple content types, with an explicit lax-proto mode.
Server-function dispatch requires matching query hash/X-QRL and application/qwik-json, validates argument-array shape, and masks ordinary execution failures with an Invalid request response.
Internal full-path headers must be relative absolute-path forms under the loader prefix; scheme-relative paths, foreign origins, and malformed URLs are rejected.
limitRequestBody validates a positive safe integer and enforces a 10 MiB default by counting streamed bytes; Node middleware combines configured and caller-supplied limits using the smaller value.
Loader result caching excludes redirect, error, and failed-result envelopes; developer-provided cache keys still define which successful serialized responses share cache entries.
Scaffolding can clear an existing target directory under --force, write outside the repository into an absolute outDir, and invoke package-manager install through execa.

MCP inspection guards its HTTP endpoint with loopback address, bearer token, absent Origin, exact Host, POST-only handling, and an 8192-byte request limit; discovery files use restrictive creation modes.

Insights dashboard middleware requires a session email, but the inspected telemetry handler accepts a validated publicApiKey payload and permits auto-creation; schema validation is not itself proof of application ownership authorization.
Insights sends its OK response before database operations finish, and counter-update comments explicitly accept missed-update risk from avoiding transactions.

Hypothesis: first-insert delay histograms may use the wrong bucket because updateEdge increments delayBucketField(edge.latencyBucket), while existing-row updates use edge.delayBucket. This source inconsistency was not reproduced.
The root Dockerfile uses Node 16.12.0 and a network-fetched Rust installer, whereas the root manifest requires Node >=22.18.0; the CLI's checkNodeVersion also retains older Node thresholds.

Docs deployment is a privileged workflow_run artifact boundary: the job checks repository identity and artifact presence, but the inspected gating does not require workflow_run.conclusion == success despite the header comment.

extension_points.summary: Extension mechanisms generally use explicit factories, branded functions, package exports, or declarative metadata. Runtime APIs and serializers connect to an optimizer-aware public boundary, while Router discovers middleware and data functions from route modules. Scaffolding discovers packaged integrations and composes them through a staged update interface. Tooling provides additional named registries for experiments, lint rules, and MCP tools.

claims.claim: core/index.ts is the public export boundary for components, QRLs, hooks, state primitives, and control-flow helpers; new public APIs must fit this export surface.
setPlatform and CorePlatform provide a named platform abstraction, while createQwikPlugin accepts an injected _optimizer before selecting built-in optimizer providers.
ExperimentalFeatures is an explicit registry for compiler-replaced runtime flags, including control-flow primitives, validation, SPA behavior, Insights, and nonblocking loaders.
routeLoaderQrl produces frozen server_loader functions carrying QRL, validators, ID, serialization strategy, cache-control, ETag, cache-key, search, and blockSSR metadata.
routeActionQrl produces frozen server_action functions; resolveRequestHandlers discovers loaders/actions by examining branded exported functions in route modules.
Route modules extend request execution through onRequest and method-specific onGet/onPost/onPut/onPatch/onDelete/onOptions/onHead handlers, each accepting a function or function array.
qwikRouter builds a plugin array around router, server-function, and image plugins; ssgAdapter composes the shared viteAdapter with origin and SSG options.
loadIntegrations discovers app, feature, and adapter directories and reads package __qwik__ metadata for display name, documentation, priority, and alwaysInRoot rules.
makeTemplateManager separates standalone templates from base and treats library as a standalone bootstrap; updateApp returns staged updates plus a commit callback.
Custom serialization APIs include useSerializer$ and createSerializer$; an inspected test supplies serialize/deserialize functions for a custom class.
The ESLint plugin uses a rules table with recommended/strict severity maps, while createMcpServer defines tools through a named table of schemas and accepts an external call dispatcher.

agent_handoff.summary: Tests and CI were inspected, not executed, and this report is a bounded source inventory rather than exhaustive coverage or a verification certificate. Future work should begin at the package and protocol boundary implicated by the task. Serialization and routing changes require coordinated reader/writer inspection, while optimizer behavior must account for both implementations. Repository setup and verification guidance is recorded below for later authorized work; none of those commands ran here.

claims.claim: Read root AGENTS.md and the owning package sources first; the monorepo map identifies core, Router, React, utilities, DOM, Vite integration, optimizers, scaffolding, docs, and Insights.
Shared guidance originates in .ruler; generated AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md should not be edited directly, and the inspected ruler-check workflow regenerates and checks their drift.
The documented focused loop is build.core.dev followed by the closest Vitest test or Chromium Playwright file; this audit inspected that guidance without executing its setup or verification commands.

Optimizer selection differs between local test configuration and default provider selection; account for tsOptimizer:true, QWIK_OPTIMIZER overrides, and Rust binding prerequisites when planning authorized checks.

For state changes, read serialization.md, SSR emitStateData, and DomContainer's reader together; preserve type/value pairing, shared references, and the distinction between qwik/state and sync-function metadata.
For action/loader protocol changes, inspect both server handlers and client transport; JSON-looking endpoints use Qwik serialization and have explicit invalidation, redirect, and caching semantics.
Loader behavior tests consume built qwikloader.debug.js, so source-only edits without regenerated output can leave the intended verification testing stale artifacts.
Root tsc.check is not a substitute for every package's type checks: tsconfig.json explicitly excludes packages/qwik/src, scripts, and generated library trees.
Preserve compatibility boundaries: qwikCity delegates to qwikRouter, staticAdapter aliases ssgAdapter, and Node notFound is a deprecated pass-through slated for V3 removal.
Do not assume repository scripts are read-only: build/update scripts generate artifacts, scaffold commit writes files, and installDeps starts an external package manager.
